narrative_flow.action_title: Cybersecurity has long depended on scarce human expertise — SCIS 2026 revealed that the field is now crossing a tipping point.
narrative_flow.purpose: Set the Situation (manual expert work is the bottleneck) and Complication (AI and formal methods are disrupting this model), framing the core question: what should researchers do now?

narrative_flow.action_title: SCIS 2026 at a glance: AI sessions drew standing-room-only crowds, signaling a paradigm shift in security research.
narrative_flow.purpose: Give the audience a vivid, concrete snapshot of the conference atmosphere to establish credibility and urgency.

narrative_flow.action_title: LLM agents have evolved from passive assistants into autonomous actors that execute multi-step security tasks.
narrative_flow.purpose: Introduce the first major trend — the qualitative leap in what AI agents can do in security.

narrative_flow.action_title: Waseda/RIKEN's CHASE project and NPA's binary analysis show agents compressing months of expert work into hours.
narrative_flow.purpose: Provide concrete evidence for the AI-agent claim with specific SCIS 2026 presentations and benchmarks.

narrative_flow.action_title: Building these agents is hard — reaching practical accuracy took 4–5 months of iterative debugging.
narrative_flow.purpose: Add realism and credibility by acknowledging the engineering difficulty, using the presenter's own experience and the CHASE project anecdote.

narrative_flow.action_title: Formal verification has matured from theory to practice, replacing hope-based assurance with machine-checked proofs.
narrative_flow.purpose: Introduce the second major trend — formal verification crossing into real-world applicability.

narrative_flow.action_title: NTT, Ibaraki University, and U. Tokyo demonstrated formally verified cryptographic implementations at SCIS 2026.
narrative_flow.purpose: Provide concrete evidence with specific case studies of formal verification catching defects that testing missed.

narrative_flow.action_title: Post-quantum cryptography has moved from theory to standardization, creating an urgent migration timeline.
narrative_flow.purpose: Introduce the third major trend — PQC is no longer future speculation but a present-day engineering challenge.

narrative_flow.action_title: With 8+ dedicated sessions and active ML-KEM/ML-DSA optimization work, PQC dominated SCIS 2026's agenda.
narrative_flow.purpose: Show the scale of PQC activity at the conference and the 'harvest now, decrypt later' urgency.

narrative_flow.action_title: These three trends are converging — AI agents accelerate formal verification and PQC migration workflows.
narrative_flow.purpose: Present the synthesis argument: the real power comes from combining these capabilities.

narrative_flow.action_title: Researchers who combine AI agents, formal verification, and PQC expertise will hold a compounding advantage.
narrative_flow.purpose: Deliver the core call to action — this is not about choosing one specialty but integrating across domains.

narrative_flow.action_title: The researchers who act on this shift now will define the next era of cybersecurity.
narrative_flow.purpose: Close with the governing argument's core message, leaving the audience with a clear, memorable takeaway and motivation to act.

passes_skim_test.justification: Reading the 12 action titles in sequence tells a complete story: (1) the field faces a tipping point, (2) SCIS 2026 proved it, (3-5) AI agents are now autonomous and powerful but hard to build, (6-7) formal verification is production-ready, (8-9) PQC is urgent and dominant, (10-11) these trends converge and reward cross-domain researchers, (12) act now or fall behind. The narrative flows from situation through evidence to call-to-action.

respects_constraints.justification: The blueprint contains 12 slides, within the hard constraint of 15 slides maximum. At roughly 75 seconds per slide, 12 slides fit comfortably within the 15-minute time limit.

has_dedicated_situation_slide.justification: Slides 1 and 2 together establish the Situation (manual expert work is the bottleneck in cybersecurity), the Complication (AI and formal methods are disrupting the status quo — standing-room-only crowds at AI sessions), and the implicit Question (what should researchers do about this shift?).
